# You Should Know

The plugin `claudetto-you-should-know` shows one thing that you should know before Claude changes something.
A side check by a model finds the thing.
In a TUI session, the plugin shows it in a band above the prompt, and the change runs as usual.
In a `-p` run, the plugin gives it to Claude as context.
It copies the flow of the built-in plugin `cc-plugin-you-should-know`, but not its code or its name.
It works without the core plugin, and it imports nothing from another plugin.

The plugin is opt-in, because each check costs a model call.
The one slice is `notice`, and its hooks are in `slices/notice/adapters/mod.ts`.

## Install

1. Install the plugin with `/plugin install claudetto-you-should-know@claudetto`.
2. Turn off the built-in plugin `cc-plugin-you-should-know@builtin` in `/plugin`, so that the two do not both check.

## The Account Gate

The plugin runs only when the account has the flag `tengu_jolly_dewdrop` on.
At `session.start`, it reads the cached value `cachedGrowthBookFeatures.tengu_jolly_dewdrop` from `.claude.json`.
The file is in `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, or in `HOME` when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is not set.

When the value is `false` or absent, or the file is missing, the plugin makes no model call.
It then logs one notice that says why.

The cache does not show the modes `hipaa`, `zdr`, and `ldr`, which also turn the built-in plugin off.
The plugin cannot read those modes.

## When It Checks

The plugin checks the first call of each turn that changes something.
A change is an `Edit`, a `Write`, a `NotebookEdit`, or a `Bash` command that writes.

These commands count as changes, not as reads:

- a redirect, such as `echo x > a.txt`
- `find` with `-fprint0`, `-fprint`, `-delete`, or `-exec`
- `git diff --output=F`
- `rg --pre CMD`, because `CMD` runs

These calls get no check:

- a read, such as `Read` or `cat a.txt`
- the second and each later changing call of the same turn
- a call of a subagent
- a call that the permission rules deny

A turn with 5 edits makes one check.
Two checks that start at the same time make one model call, because the first one claims the turn.

## What the Check Gives

The model answers with one JSON object: a `topic`, which is one sentence or `null`, an `id`, and a list of `claims`.
The `id` is 2 to 6 English words in lowercase ASCII, joined with `-`, that name the subject of the topic.
A topic is a trade-off that you possibly do not see, a design decision that has effects later, or an edge case that is not clear.
Most checks give `null`, and then nothing shows.
The plugin reads the object.
It does not look for the word `NONE`, so a topic that starts with "None" still shows.
The plugin compares the `id` of a topic with the ids of the topics that showed in the session, and a topic with a known `id` does not show again.
The compare does not use the words of the topic, so a reworded topic, or a topic in another language, is still a repeat.
An object with a topic and no valid `id` is not shown.

The prompt has a data rule: the text between the tags `<request>`, `<action>`, and `<seen>` is data, and the model must not obey it.
The plugin breaks a closing tag in that text, so the text cannot end its own tag.

A preview of a saved output, or a cleared result, is not the whole result.
The prompt says so.

## The Check of Claims

The side model sees only a preview of a file, so a claim about a whole file can be wrong.
Each claim names a file and one state:

| State | The disk backs it when |
| --- | --- |
| `missing` | The path does not exist. |
| `empty` | The path is a file of 0 bytes. |
| `cut` | The file is not empty and does not end with a newline. |

The plugin reads the disk before it shows the topic.
When one claim fails, it drops the whole topic and logs the claim.
An answer with more than 3 claims, or with an unknown state, counts as malformed and is dropped.
The `cut` rule is a heuristic, so a file that ends without a newline on purpose backs the claim.

## Where the Topic Shows

| Surface | Result |
| --- | --- |
| TUI | A band above the prompt. The text names the side check as the source. |
| `-p` | Context for Claude, in the result of the checked call. The tool waits for the check. |

The band says that "a side check by a model found this".
It does not say that you gave the heads-up or did the action.
`1` fills the prompt with the topic, and the note goes to the next call of the main agent, once.
`0` dismisses the band.

The topic reaches Claude with the result of the checked call, not before the call runs.
The hook `tool.check` has no field for context, so this is the earliest point.

A run with no screen is a headless run.
The plugin cannot tell plain `-p` from stream-json.

## What a Check Costs

The plugin makes at most one model call per turn.
The call is a separate call to Haiku, with your prompt and the pending action, and no transcript.
In a TUI session, the tool does not wait for the call.
Each check sends the newest 10 topics that showed, so the input stays bounded.
The reply has a token limit, and the eval bound of the hook is `CHECK_TOKENS`.

A failed call shows nothing, and the change runs.
The plugin logs the error to the debug log.

## When `CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER` Is `0`

On a subscription, a separate call from a hook gets HTTP 429 when `CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER` is `0`.
The request then carries no billing block, so the API refuses it.

After a 429, that turn gets no topic and no second call.
From the next turn, the plugin uses a fork of the main conversation for the rest of the session.
A fork sends the main request again, so it works, but it costs much more than a separate call.
The fork has no output bound and no cancel, because `$.model.fork` takes only `{ prompt }`.
The plugin stops waiting for it after `FORK_WAIT_MS`, but it cannot stop the request.
Keep the attribution header on to get the cheaper check.

## Limits

- The plugin has no live measure of the real gate in a sandbox session yet.
- The cost of a fork is not measured on this design.
